subject: logistics-supply-chain
intro: Logistics and supply chain study leads to the people who keep goods moving — planning what to buy, where to hold it, and how to get it to customers on time and at cost.

roles.title: Logisticians
roles.what: Analyse and coordinate the ongoing logistical functions of a firm — managing the whole life cycle of a product, from acquisition, distribution and internal allocation to delivery and final disposal of resources.
roles.where: Unit 1's end-to-end chain and SCOR metrics frame the analysis; unit 3's inventory policies, unit 5's capacity and scheduling and unit 6's transportation modes, warehousing and last-mile delivery are the day-to-day levers.

roles.title: Supply Chain Managers
roles.what: Direct or coordinate production, purchasing, warehousing, distribution or forecasting activities to limit costs and improve accuracy, customer service or safety — streamlining procedures and directing the movement, storage and processing of inventory.
roles.where: Units 2, 3 and 5 — demand forecasting, inventory policy and production operations — are the functions they direct; unit 6's network design and unit 8's risk and resilience strategies shape how they build the chain.

roles.title: Purchasing Managers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree plus years of experience
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the work of buyers and purchasing officers — sourcing the materials, products and services an organisation needs, choosing suppliers and managing the contracts behind them.
roles.where: Unit 4 is the direct match: sourcing strategies, supplier selection and contracts, and the ethics and risk of sourcing; unit 7's global sourcing and tariffs plus Incoterms extend the toolkit to international procurement.

roles.title: Operations Research Analysts
roles.what: Formulate and apply mathematical modelling and other optimising methods to assist management with decisions — collecting and analysing data and developing optimal time, cost or logistics networks for programmes and operations.
roles.where: Unit 2's forecasting methods and error analysis and unit 3's EOQ and safety-stock arithmetic are classic optimisation problems; unit 8's digital supply chain — AI, IoT and analytics — is where their models get deployed.
